# manual capture: NDEBUG emulation -- the Debug assert and the reporter's Release access
#                 violation are the same defect
# compiler: main-debug  (<repo>\build\Debug\bin\dxc.exe)
# version:  dxcompiler.dll: 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433) - 1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907)
# harness:  ndebug-emulate.cmd   (cdb 10.0.26100.6584, x64)  -- re-runnable
# ran:      2026-08-07
# NOTE:     hand-driven capture, not a probe. Not scored by match.json.
#           Trimmed by trim-cdb.py; module-load and symbol-path noise removed.
#
# WHY
# The ground-truth build is a Debug build and stops at a DXASSERT, while @Dwedit reported an
# access violation from a release dxcompiler. Those could be two different things. `gh` in cdb
# steps over a __debugbreak() and continues, which is exactly what a build with
# DXASSERT compiled out (include/dxc/Support/Global.h:356, `do { } while (0)`) would do -- so
# this run answers "what does the release build do?" without building one.
#
# WHAT IT SHOWS
# Two asserts fire and are stepped over:
#     ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp(4791)  !(argIdx < endArgIdx)      "arg index out of bound"
#     ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp(4801)  !(matrix.Orientation == MatrixOrientation::ColumnMajor)
# The second is itself a consequence of the first: line 4792 indexes FlatAnnotationList out of
# bounds, so `paramAnnotation` is whatever heap bytes follow the vector, and those bytes claim
# a matrix annotation with a nonsense orientation.
#
# Execution then reaches c0000374 (STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION) and finally dies on an access
# violation inside memcpy, under:
#     std::vector<unsigned int>::_Emplace_reallocate
#     hlsl::DxilParameterAnnotation::AppendSemanticIndex
#     AllocateSemanticIndex  (x4, recursive)
#     SROA_Parameter_HLSL::allocateSemanticIndex
#     SROA_Parameter_HLSL::flattenArgument
# which is @Dwedit's 2021 stack frame for frame, including his note that it "crashes in a
# memory copy". So this is NOT an NDEBUG artefact: with the assert compiled out the bad index
# is simply used, and that is what the 20 release binaries do (see manual-case-crash-form.txt
# and the out-v*.txt probes).
